reviews.title: Ew
reviews.text: I submitted a formal request for the deletion of my personal information under the Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act (MCDPA). Unfortunately, the developer has failed to respond or provide confirmation that my data has been deleted.  Under Minnesota Statutes § 325M.14, Subdivision 1(d), consumers have the right to request deletion of their personal data.  Additionally, Minnesota Statutes § 325M.14, Subdivision 4(e)–(f) requires covered businesses to respond to consumer privacy requests within 45 days, including providing reasons if they refuse to act. An extension of up to 45 additional days is permitted when reasonably necessary, provided the consumer is notified within the initial 45-day period.

My only complaint is the chat scroll is sensitive and hard to control but the chat itself is just like chat rooms of the early internet- they’re off the chain! The monetized aspect is not going to help you pay any bills but it is an incentive to get out there and let your community know what’s up. I’ve realized a lot of people can’t leave the house and want know what’s happening and it feels kind of nice to put minds to rest. Highly recommend! @ChatsworthChisme

reviews.title: Will not allow you to cancel subscription
reviews.text:
(Edited to add: I contacted the Better Business Bureau, filed a complaint, and I encourage everyone else having this issue to do the same. This is unacceptable.)

The concept is cool, and overall it’s a cool app. I can’t justify $20/month for it and to top it off, if you signed up with your Apple ID, it’s impossible to cancel your subscription. It directed me to their website with “Stripe” to sign up. So, I have to use the app to manage my subscription, not my Apple settings. The “cancel subscription” button is hidden behind the navigation window and will not allow you to select it. 
Since I used my Apple ID and not my email, I don’t even know the sign up email to try to use their website. It’s not located on the app anywhere, not even under my account settings. 

Customer service is NO help. It’s just an AI bot or automated messaging system that sends you the same steps they have on their website. No actual help. 

This may be an app design flaw but it left a negative impression for me. Like I said, the app and concept are really cool but there’s some major design flaws that are really inconvenient for users. I will be upset if this doesn’t get resolved before the next billing cycle. 

Do better, Citizen. Users should not have this much difficulty getting out of a subscription.

reviews.title: Cancel Subscription Button in-app hidden
reviews.text:
Following the instructions — the global navigation bar at the bottom is overlaid on the “Cancel Subscription” button. So you literally cannot tap the button to cancel the subscription within the app. This is absolutely against the Apple App Store TOS.  

Here’s the instructions from the help center. Apple’s App Store review team should validate and block this app for violations. 

If You Subscribed via the Website (Stripe)

Open the Citizen app and tap your Profile icon in the top right corner of the Map tab.
In your Profile, go to App Settings.
Tap Manage Subscription.
Enter the email address associated with your subscription. If it’s correct, you’ll receive an email with a link to your Customer Portal.
In the Customer Portal, tap Cancel Subscription to stop your subscription from auto-renewing.
